judgment.rationale: First (Topic '1. Addition', Theme BASIC OPERATIONS) is 'add 2-digit whole numbers with sum not greater than 40 without exchanging or renaming'; second (Topic '5. Whole Numbers 1-99', Theme NUMBER AND NUMERATION) is 'write correctly the numbers 1-99'. Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives (rank 0). Substantively, proficiency in reading/writing numbers to 99 is a numeration foundation that supports operating on 2-digit numbers (sums to 40 lie within 1-99), so the numeration skill supports success in 2-digit addition. This is a developmental support, not mere shared wording; the token overlap ('numbers','pupils','should','be','able','to') is largely generic and does not by itself establish the link. Direction second_to_first: writing numbers 1-99 builds toward adding 2-digit numbers.

producer_judgment.rationale: The second SFI (PRIMARY ONE, rank 0) asks pupils to identify and name 3D shapes including cuboids and cubes; the first SFI (PRIMARY TWO, rank 1) extends this to identifying real-world home objects that are cuboids and cubes. Both sit in the same Theme (Mensuration and Geometry), Sub-Theme (Shapes), and Topic (Three dimensional shapes). Proficiency in recognizing and naming the 3D shapes supports the later application of recognizing those shapes in everyday objects, a lower-to-higher grade developmental progression, so buildsTowards second_to_first is warranted over symmetric relatesTo.
